Akpatok Island lies in its namesake bay, and the islands of Nottingham, Salsibury and Mansel lie just offshore of it. The Hudson Strait separates this from Baffin Island, while to its west lies Hudson Bay, for 20 points, name this peninsula of northern Quebec.

John Gabriel Stedman wrote an account of his five year experience in this place, and a massacre occurred in this nation at the village of Moiwana in 1986 between the Junglecommandos of Ronnie Brunswick and the forces of Desi Bouterse. The Aluku and Kwinti peoples of this nation speak dialects of the creole language Ndyuka, and the Tumuk Humak Mountains stretch across its southeast. Francis Willoughby was the first European to establish a colony here, although its capture by Abraham Crijnssen resulted in it being transferred to another nation through the Treaty of Breda. The river which forms most of this nation's western border begins in the Acarai Mountains and creates King George VI Falls, while the Litani is a tributary of the river which forms its eastern border. Nestled between the Courantyne River on the west and the Maroni on the east, this nation's center is defined by its largest lake, the Brokopondo Reservoir or Professor ► van Blommestein Meer. Inhabited mainly by the descendants of South Asians and Maroons, identify this South American nation, a former colony of the Netherlands located between Guyana and French Guiana, with capital at Paramaraibo.

The Chalcalburnus tarichi or Pearl Mullet are the only fish known to inhabit this body of water, and its namesake breed of cat is often odd eyed. The Ktuts monastery once stood on its Carpanak Island, and the Cathedral of the Holy Cross was built by King Gagik I Artsruni on its Akdamar Island. The city of Tushpa, which served as the capital of Urartu, lies on the banks of this body of water, and the Ahlatshahs had their namesake capital on its shores. This lake has no outlet to the sea because of the eruption of Mount Nemrut, and its northern edge is dominated by Mount Suphan. With Urmia and Sevan, this lake once formed one of the "three seas of Armenia". For 20 points, name this endorheic saline body of water, the largest lake in Turkey.

Jean Clottes claims that the valley of this river's tributary, the Coa, contains Europe's largest open air site of Paleolithic art, and its Maria Pia Bridge was built by Gustave Eiffel. A tributary of this river gives its name to the aristocratic family which was accused of attempting to assassinate King Joseph I in the 1750s, and its Pisuerga River tributary flows through Valladolid. The main industry of lands around this river was devastated by the influx of Phylloxera and Powdery mildew in the 19th century, although that industry was helped by the earlier Methuen Treaty. Among the historically important names associated with this river are the aforementioned tributary, the Tavora, and the cities of Braganza and Tordesillas which lie on it. Beginning in the Soria Province, this river flows through the meseta plateau region before flowing through Vila Nova de Gaia and ► another city at its mouth. Name this Iberian river which begins in Spain and reaches the Atlantic at Porto.

Endangered species such as the Great Indian Bustard and Siberian Crane can be found in this state's Keoladeo National Park while its Ranthambore and Sariska parks serve as tiger reserves. The Luni River begins in the Aravalli Range of this state, which also contains its highest peak, Mount Abu, whose Dilwara Temples are a sight of pilgrimage for Jains. This state contains the western half of the Kathiarbar-Gir dry deciduous forest, and its city of its city of Kalibangan along the Ghaggar River was the site of the world's first ploughed field. Its ruler Rana Sanga was defeated by Babur at the Battle of Khanwa, and that outcome was repeated at the Battle of Haldighati in which one of Akbar's general's defeated Pratap Singh, a ruler of this state's Mewar region. One of the cities in this state contains a palace on Lake Pichola which was prominently featured in Octopussy, and this state's Amber Fort overlooks a city in which lies a structure representing the crown of Krishna, the Hawa Mahal or "Palace of Winds". With cities including Udaipur, Jodhpur and the capital ► Jaipur, identify this largest state of India, whose Thar Desert extends into Gujarat and Pakistan.

Operation Cherry Blossom took place in this island's Empress Augusta Bay, and this island was one of the main objectives of Operation Cartwheel. A secessionist movement here protested the copper mines at Panguna, which were operated by a subsidiary company of Rio Tonto, and in putting it down, the government enlisted the help of a mercenary company called Sandline International. The leader of that rebellion, Francis Ona, proclaimed himself the King of Meekamui shortly before his death in 2005. Mount Balbi is the highest point of its Emperor Range, and its namesake province includes the Carteret Islands and Buka. With capital at Arawa, name this island owned by Papua New Guinea, the largest of the Solomons, which is named after a French explorer of the Pacific.

Against the wishes of Ernest Bevin, it was agreed that this feature would not pass through the towns of Sagan and Lauban along the Kwisa and Bober rivers, and it was also unsuccessfully proposed that this feature should be moved westward to include the city of Bautzen, the center of the Sorbs. A treaty officially recognizing this feature was agreed upon in the cities of Zgorzelec and Gorlitz, and it was referred to as "political dynamite" by Harry Hopkins. Two towns named Gubin, one spelled with an "e", the other with an "i", are located on opposite sides of this feature, and the Battle of Seelow Heights is usually incorporated into a larger offensive which shares its name with this. Upon the agreement on this feature, one nation received Stettin and ► Gdansk, but Konigsberg was given to their eastern neighbor. Finally agreed upon at the Potsdam Conference, name this line which forms the border between Poland and Germany, named after a major river and its tributary.

Friar Inigo Abbad wrote the first history of the people of this island, whose first inhabitants were the Ortoiroid peoples. This island's Anasco River was the site of the drowning of Diego Salcedo by Urayoan and Agueybana, two local caciques who wanted to prove that the Spaniards were not gods. Milwaukee Deep is the deepest part of its namesake trench, and the El Toro Wilderness is contained within its El Yunque National Forest. His organization of the Grito de Lares and years spent fighting for its independence resulted in Ramon Betances gaining the title "Father" of this place, and it was industrialized by Operation Bootstrap following World War Two. The subject of the Jones and ► Foraker acts, this territory's island of Vieques was once used as a bombing range. With cities like Mayaguez and Arecibo, name this Caribbean island territory of the United States east of Hispaniola whose capital is San Juan.

This country's city of Albreda was once a French enclave, and an attempt to colonize it was made by Jacob Kettler, the Duke of Courland, in the 17th century. In 2008, the president of this nation gave a final ultimatum to homosexuals in his country in a speech at Tallinding, saying that if they stayed, he would cut off their heads. That dictator, Yahya Jammeh, has ruled this nation since 1994, and its capital was once named after the man who succeeded George Canning in his first term as Foreign Secretary, Henry Bathurst. This country's namesake river flows through Niokolo-Koba National Park before entering it at Fatoto, and the river begins in the Fouta Djallon. With largest city at ► Serrekunda, name this phallic-shaped country of Western Africa surrounded by Senegal, whose capital is Banjul.

Homer's Alcinous ruled the Phaiakians on the island of Scheria, which many modern scholars identify as this island, and its Achilleion Palace was built by Sissi after the death of her son in the Mayerling Affair. This island's namesake strait is connected to Lake Butrint by the Vivari Channel, and it lies only two nautical miles off the coast of Sarande. Although it was transferred to France in the Treaty of Campo Formio, under Venetian control this island was never captured by the Ottomans, due in large part to the tactics of Johann Mathias von der Schulenburg, and the defenses of the Angelokastro. This island is the namesake of two ► international incidents, one of which involved the murder of an Italian general in 1923, while the other involved the Royal Navy engaging Albanians on three separate occasions in 1946, an early part of the Cold War. The namesake of a prefecture which includes the islands of Mathraki, Othonoi and Paxos, name this second largest of the Greek Ionian Islands.

This entity once claimed the territory of Chamizal, and it ceded the Horcon Tract around the city of Rio Rico to its southern neighbor in 1970. The city of New Braunfels was founded here as part of Adelsverein, a failed attempt to create a German colony in the 1840s and a Karankawa raid doomed Robert De La Salle's attempt to colonize this in the 1680s. The shipwreck of the Narvaez expedition and Cabeza de Vaca eventually led to the colonization of this region, and the Battle of Goliad was part of the conflict in which it became an independent republic with capital at ► Washington-on-the-Bravos. Name this state which has been ruled by itself, France, Spain, the Confederacy and Mexico, as well as the United States.

The kingdoms of Dali and Nanzhao were centered in this region, and its Lake Dian was used as the model for an artificial lake in Beijing's Summer Palace. This region is home to the "Fortunate Victory Prayer Wheel", a structure in bas-relief that represents its nation's 56 ethnic groups, and pilgrims travel to this region to take the two week-long kora around its Mount Kawagebo, which features the Ganden Suntseling Monastery. The aforementioned features are located near this region's town of Zhongdian, whose name has recently been changed to Shangri-La in an attempt to attract tourists to nearby Pudacuo National Park as well as the ► Three Parallel Rivers region. With capital at Kunming, name this Chinese province, the source of the Mekong and Yangtze rivers, which borders Sichuan and Tibet as well as Burma, Laos and Vietnam.

This city features the Oscar Niemeyer-designed Volcan Cultural Center, and its post-war reconstruction by Auguste Perret, the teacher of Le Corbusier, made this city one of the few contemporary UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Lying in the Pays de Caux region, this city was the objective of Operation Astonia, and its citizens renamed it after Jean-Paul Marat for two years during the Revolution. This city was first named after Francis I, who founded it to replace the nearby ports of Honfleur and Harfleur. The setting for Monet's ► Impression, Sunrise, name this port city of Normandy at the mouth of the Seine.

This country's Plateau of the Rivers is it's only natural UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the five qsur of its M'zab region form an urban conglomerate known as Pentapolis. This nation contains Roman ruins at Timgad and Djemila, while the Tademait Plateau lies north of its city of In Salah. Tamanrasset is the chief city in the south of this nation, and Mount Tahat is the highest peak of its Ahaggar Mountains. This nation contains the Aures and Tell ranges of the ► Atlas Mountains, and its main cities include Annaba, Constantine and Oran. The center of the Maghreb, name this nation of North Africa between Tunisia and Morocco.

One writer associated with this place wrote Desultory Thoughts in London and Titus and Gisippus after having a major nervous breakdown which caused him to show up at another writer's place claiming to be the devil. Another writer associated with this place wrote Recolleections of a Tour made in Scotland, kept an extremely important journal, and was written of in a poem as having "shooting lights" in her "wild eyes." Another writer associated with this place was an essayist who wrote a highly laudatory "Discourse on the English Mail Carriage." Yet another writer associated with this place wrote about a simoom in his ► "Thalaba the Destroyer" and another poem in which little Peterkin enquires about the efficacy of a certain battle in "After Blenheim." identify this place associated with poets like Robert Southey and the authors of Lyrical Ballads, Samuel Taylor Coleridge and William Wordsworth.

The Emigrant and Hoover Wildernesses are adjacent to this region, and the Clark and Cathedral ranges run through it. Lafayette Bunnell was one of the first to explore and write about this place, and the O'Shaghnessy Dam has created a reservoir in this park's Hetch Hetchy Valley. The Ahwahneechee tribe believed that the spirit Pohono lived in this park's Bridalveil Fall, and it contains the valleys of the Tuolumne and Merced rivers. This park features Half Dome, and The Nose is a famous climbing route to the top of its El Capitan. Conserved largely from the efforts of ► John Muir, name this national park of the Sierra Nevadas located largely in Mariposa County, California.
